metadata.title: The entropy formula for the Ricci flow and its geometric applications
metadata.author: Grisha Perelman

nodes.name: Ricci flow equation
nodes.statement: The Ricci flow is the evolution equation $\frac{d}{dt}g_{ij}(t) = -2R_{ij}$ for a riemannian metric $g_{ij}(t)$ on a closed manifold $M$.
nodes.statement_clean: The evolution equation for a Riemannian metric driven by minus twice the Ricci tensor.

nodes.name: Functional $\cF$
nodes.statement: $\cF = \int_M (R + |\nabla f|^2) e^{-f} dV$ for a riemannian metric $g_{ij}$ and a function $f$ on a closed manifold $M$.
nodes.statement_clean: An entropy-like functional combining scalar curvature and the gradient of a potential.

nodes.name: Breather
nodes.statement: A metric $g_{ij}(t)$ evolving by the Ricci flow is called a breather if for some $t_1 < t_2$ and $\alpha > 0$ the metrics $\alpha g_{ij}(t_1)$ and $g_{ij}(t_2)$ differ only by a diffeomorphism. Cases $\alpha=1, \alpha<1, \alpha>1$ are steady, shrinking, expanding.

nodes.name: Ricci soliton
nodes.statement: A trivial breather, where the metrics $g_{ij}(t_1)$ and $g_{ij}(t_2)$ differ only by diffeomorphism and scaling for each pair $t_1, t_2$. Satisfies $R_{ij} + cg_{ij} + \nabla_i b_j + \nabla_j b_i = 0$.
nodes.statement_clean: A self-similar solution of the Ricci flow that is fixed up to diffeomorphism and scaling.

nodes.name: Lambda invariant $\lambda(g_{ij})$
nodes.statement: $\lambda(g_{ij}) = \inf \cF(g_{ij}, f)$ where the infimum is taken over all smooth $f$ satisfying $\int_M e^{-f} dV = 1$. Equals the lowest eigenvalue of $-4\triangle + R$.

nodes.name: Functional $\cW$ (entropy)
nodes.statement: $\cW(g_{ij}, f, \tau) = \int_M [\tau(|\nabla f|^2 + R) + f - n](4\pi\tau)^{-n/2} e^{-f} dV$ restricted to $f$ with $\int_M (4\pi\tau)^{-n/2} e^{-f} dV = 1$, $\tau > 0$.
nodes.statement_clean: A scale-aware entropy functional generalizing $\cF$ used to handle the shrinking case.

nodes.name: Mu and nu invariants
nodes.statement: $\mu(g_{ij}, \tau) = \inf \cW(g_{ij}, f, \tau)$ over smooth $f$ satisfying the constraint, and $\nu(g_{ij}) = \inf_{\tau>0} \mu(g_{ij}, \tau)$.

nodes.name: Locally collapsing
nodes.statement: $g_{ij}(t)$ is locally collapsing at $T$ if there is a sequence $t_k \to T$ and metric balls $B_k = B(p_k, r_k)$ at times $t_k$ such that $r_k^2/t_k$ is bounded, $|Rm|(g_{ij}(t_k)) \le r_k^{-2}$ in $B_k$, and $r_k^{-n} Vol(B_k) \to 0$.

nodes.name: $\kappa$-noncollapsed metric
nodes.statement: A metric $g_{ij}$ is $\kappa$-noncollapsed on the scale $\rho$ if every metric ball $B$ of radius $r < \rho$ satisfying $|Rm|(x) \le r^{-2}$ for every $x \in B$ has volume at least $\kappa r^n$.

nodes.name: $\mathcal{L}$-length
nodes.statement: For a curve $\gamma(\tau)$, $0 < \tau_1 \le \tau \le \tau_2$, $\mathcal{L}(\gamma) = \int_{\tau_1}^{\tau_2} \sqrt{\tau}(R(\gamma(\tau)) + |\dot\gamma(\tau)|^2) d\tau$.
nodes.statement_clean: A weighted action functional on space-time curves used to define a comparison geometry for the backward Ricci flow.

nodes.name: Reduced distance $l(q,\tau)$
nodes.statement: $l(q,\tau) = \frac{1}{2\sqrt{\tau}} L(q,\tau)$, where $L(q,\bar\tau)$ is the $\mathcal{L}$-length of the $\mathcal{L}$-shortest curve from $p$ to $q$ over $[0,\bar\tau]$.

nodes.name: Reduced volume $\tilde V(\tau)$
nodes.statement: $\tilde V(\tau) = \int_M \tau^{-n/2} \exp(-l(q,\tau)) dq$.
nodes.statement_clean: A monotone integral quantity associated to the reduced distance, decreasing in $\tau$.

nodes.name: $\kappa$-collapsed at $(x_0,t_0)$ on scale $r$
nodes.statement: A solution to the Ricci flow is $\kappa$-collapsed at $(x_0,t_0)$ on the scale $r > 0$ if $|Rm|(x,t) \le r^{-2}$ for all $(x,t)$ with $\mathrm{dist}_{t_0}(x,x_0) < r$ and $t_0 - r^2 \le t \le t_0$, and $Vol(B(x_0,r)) < \kappa r^n$.

nodes.name: $\phi$-almost nonnegative curvature
nodes.statement: A solution to the Ricci flow has $\phi$-almost nonnegative curvature if $Rm(x,t) \ge -\phi(R(x,t)) R(x,t)$ for each $(x,t)$, where $\phi$ is a decreasing function tending to zero at infinity.

nodes.name: $\epsilon$-neck
nodes.statement: A point $x_0 \in M$ is the center of an $\epsilon$-neck if the solution $g_{ij}(t)$ in $\{(x,t): -(\epsilon Q)^{-1} < t \le 0, \mathrm{dist}_0^2(x,x_0) < (\epsilon Q)^{-1}\}$, where $Q = R(x_0,0)$, is, after scaling by $Q$, $\epsilon$-close to the corresponding subset of the evolving round cylinder of scalar curvature one at $t=0$.

nodes.name: Asymptotic volume ratio $\cV$
nodes.statement: For a non-compact complete riemannian manifold of nonnegative Ricci curvature with a point $p$, $\cV = \lim_{r\to\infty} Vol(B(p,r)) r^{-n}$.

nodes.name: Upper bound on $\cF^m$
nodes.statement: If the gradient flow for $\cF^m$ exists for $t \in [0,T]$, then at $t=0$ we have $\cF^m \le \frac{n}{2T} \int_M dm$.
conclusions: $\cF^m(0) \le \frac{n}{2T} \int_M dm$

nodes.name: No local collapsing theorem I
nodes.statement: If $M$ is closed and $T < \infty$, then $g_{ij}(t)$ is not locally collapsing at $T$.
assumptions: $g_{ij}(t)$ smooth solution to Ricci flow on $[0,T)$
conclusions: $g_{ij}(t)$ is not locally collapsing at $T$

nodes.name: $\kappa$-noncollapsing of blow-up limits
nodes.statement: If $|Rm|(x,t) \le CQ_k$ whenever $t<t_k$ with $Q_k=|Rm|(p_k,t_k)\to\infty$, then a subsequence of scalings of $g_{ij}(t_k)$ at $p_k$ with factors $Q_k$ converges to a complete ancient solution that is $\kappa$-noncollapsed on all scales for some $\kappa>0$.
conclusions: Subsequence of rescalings converges to a complete ancient solution
Limit is $\kappa$-noncollapsed on all scales for some $\kappa>0$

nodes.name: No local collapsing theorem II
nodes.statement: For any $A > 0$ there exists $\kappa = \kappa(A) > 0$: if $g_{ij}(t)$ on $[0, r_0^2]$ has $|Rm|(x,t) \le r_0^{-2}$ for $\mathrm{dist}_0(x,x_0) < r_0$ and $Vol(B(x_0,r_0)) \ge A^{-1} r_0^n$ at $t=0$, then it cannot be $\kappa$-collapsed on scales $< r_0$ at $(x, r_0^2)$ with $\mathrm{dist}_{r_0^2}(x,x_0) \le A r_0$.
conclusions: $g_{ij}(t)$ cannot be $\kappa(A)$-collapsed on scales $< r_0$ at any $(x,r_0^2)$ with $\mathrm{dist}_{r_0^2}(x,x_0) \le A r_0$

nodes.name: Distance distortion lemma (Lemma 8.3)
nodes.statement: (a) If $\mathrm{Ric}(x,t_0) \le (n-1)K$ when $\mathrm{dist}_{t_0}(x,x_0) < r_0$, then outside $B(x_0,r_0)$, $d_t - \triangle d \ge -(n-1)(\frac{2}{3}K r_0 + r_0^{-1})$. (b) If the Ricci bound holds in both balls $B(x_0,r_0)$ and $B(x_1,r_0)$, then $\frac{d}{dt} \mathrm{dist}_t(x_0,x_1) \ge -2(n-1)(\frac{2}{3}K r_0 + r_0^{-1})$.
conclusions: Differential inequality on the distance function $d_t - \triangle d$
Lower bound on time derivative of distance between fixed points

nodes.name: Conjugate heat equation Harnack identity
nodes.statement:
If $u = (4\pi(T-t))^{-n/2} e^{-f}$ satisfies $\Box^* u = -u_t - 	riangle u + Ru = 0$, then $v = [(T-t)(2	riangle f - |
abla f|^2 + R) + f - n] u$ satisfies $\Box^* v = -2(T-t) |R_{ij} + 
abla_i 
abla_j f -  rac{1}{2(T-t)} g_{ij}|^2$.
assumptions: $u = (4\pi(T-t))^{-n/2} e^{-f}$ solves the conjugate heat equation
conclusions: $\Box^* v = -2(T-t)|R_{ij} + \nabla_i\nabla_j f - \frac{1}{2(T-t)} g_{ij}|^2$

nodes.name: Monotonicity of $\min v/u$
nodes.statement: Under assumptions of Prop. 9.1, on a closed manifold $M$ (or where the maximum principle applies), $\min v/u$ is nondecreasing in $t$.
conclusions: $\min v/u$ is nondecreasing in $t$

nodes.name: $v \le 0$ for $\delta$-function initial data
nodes.statement: Under same assumptions, if $u$ tends to a $\delta$-function as $t \to T$, then $v \le 0$ for all $t < T$.

nodes.name: Differential Harnack inequality along curves
nodes.statement: Under the previous assumptions, for any smooth curve $\gamma(t)$: $-\frac{d}{dt} f(\gamma(t),t) \le \frac{1}{2}(R(\gamma(t),t) + |\dot\gamma(t)|^2) - \frac{1}{2(T-t)} f(\gamma(t),t)$.

nodes.name: Reduced distance bounds $f$
nodes.statement: If $p$ is the point where the limit $\delta$-function is concentrated, then $f(q,t) \le l(q, T-t)$, where $l$ is the reduced distance defined in 7.1, using $p$ and $\tau(t)=T-t$.

nodes.name: Pseudolocality theorem
nodes.statement: For every $\alpha > 0$ there exist $\delta, \epsilon > 0$ such that if $g_{ij}(t)$ on $[0, (\epsilon r_0)^2]$ satisfies $R(x) \ge -r_0^{-2}$ and $Vol(\partial\Omega)^n \ge (1-\delta) c_n Vol(\Omega)^{n-1}$ at $t=0$ for $x, \Omega \subset B(x_0,r_0)$, then $|Rm|(x,t) \le \alpha t^{-1} + (\epsilon r_0)^{-2}$ when $0 < t \le (\epsilon r_0)^2$ and $\mathrm{dist}_t(x,x_0) < \epsilon r_0$.
conclusions: $|Rm|(x,t) \le \alpha t^{-1} + (\epsilon r_0)^{-2}$ for $0 < t \le (\epsilon r_0)^2$, $\mathrm{dist}_t(x,x_0) < \epsilon r_0$

nodes.name: Lower volume bound from pseudolocality
nodes.statement: Under the same assumptions as 10.1, at time $t \in (0,(\epsilon r_0)^2]$, $Vol B(x,\sqrt{t}) \ge c \sqrt{t}^n$ for $x \in B(x_0, \epsilon r_0)$, with $c = c(n)$ universal.

nodes.name: Pseudolocality variant with volume hypothesis
nodes.statement: There exist $\epsilon, \delta > 0$: if $g_{ij}(t)$ on $[0,(\epsilon r_0)^2]$ satisfies $|Rm|(x) \le r_0^{-2}$ in $B(x_0,r_0)$ and $Vol B(x_0,r_0) \ge (1-\delta) \omega_n r_0^n$ at $t=0$, then $|Rm|(x,t) \le (\epsilon r_0)^{-2}$ for $0 \le t \le (\epsilon r_0)^2$, $\mathrm{dist}_t(x,x_0) < \epsilon r_0$.
conclusions: $|Rm|(x,t) \le (\epsilon r_0)^{-2}$ for $0 \le t \le (\epsilon r_0)^2$, $\mathrm{dist}_t(x,x_0) < \epsilon r_0$

nodes.name: $\kappa$-noncollapsing under almost-Euclidean isoperimetry
nodes.statement: There exist $\epsilon, \delta > 0$ and for any $A>0$ a $\kappa(A) > 0$: with the assumptions of 10.1 and $A^{-1}(\epsilon r_0)^2 \le t \le (\epsilon r_0)^2$, $\mathrm{dist}_t(x,x_0) \le A r_0$, the solution cannot be $\kappa$-collapsed at $(x,t)$ on scales less than $\sqrt{t}$.

nodes.name: Convergence to gradient shrinking soliton
nodes.statement: The scalings of $g_{ij}(t_0 - \tau)$ at $q(\tau)$ with factors $\tau^{-1}$ converge along a subsequence of $\tau \to \infty$ to a non-flat gradient shrinking soliton.
assumptions: Ancient solution under assumptions of 11.1 ($\kappa$-noncollapsed, complete, non-flat, nonnegative curvature operator)
conclusions: Subsequence of rescalings converges to a non-flat gradient shrinking soliton

nodes.name: 2D ancient solutions are round spheres
nodes.statement: There is only one oriented two-dimensional solution satisfying assumptions of 11.1: the round sphere.

nodes.name: Vanishing asymptotic volume ratio
nodes.statement: Under assumptions of 11.1, $\cV = 0$ for each $t$.
conclusions: Asymptotic volume ratio $\cV(t) = 0$ for each $t$

nodes.name: Volume decay at large scales
nodes.statement: For every $\epsilon > 0$ there exists $A < \infty$: under appropriate ancient-solution assumptions, $Vol B(x_k, A/\sqrt{Q_k}) \le \epsilon (A/\sqrt{Q_k})^n$ at $t=0$ for large $k$.

nodes.name: Curvature bound from volume bound
nodes.statement: For every $w > 0$ there exist $B(w), C(w) < \infty$, $\tau_0(w) > 0$: (a) Under nonnegative curvature operator and $Vol B(x_0,r_0) \ge w r_0^n$ for all $t \in [t_0, 0]$, $R(x,t) \le C r_0^{-2} + B(t-t_0)^{-1}$ for $\mathrm{dist}_t(x,x_0) \le r_0/4$. (b) Same conclusion holds with $-\tau_0 r_0^2$ in place of $t_0$ if the volume bound is only assumed at $t=0$ and $-t_0 \ge \tau_0 r_0^2$.

nodes.name: Compactness of noncompact ancient solutions
nodes.statement: The set of non-compact ancient solutions in dimension three satisfying the assumptions of 11.1 is compact modulo scaling: from any sequence with $R(x_k,0)=1$ we can extract a smoothly converging subsequence whose limit satisfies the same conditions.
assumptions: Ancient solutions on noncompact oriented three-manifolds
Assumptions of 11.1 (complete, non-flat, bounded curvature, nonnegative curvature operator, $\kappa$-noncollapsed)
conclusions: The class is compact modulo scaling
Limits satisfy the same conditions

nodes.name: Necks outside a compact set
nodes.statement: For any $\epsilon > 0$ there exists $C(\epsilon,\kappa) > 0$: if $g_{ij}(t)$ satisfies 11.1 and $M_\epsilon$ denotes the set of points that are not centers of $\epsilon$-necks, then $M_\epsilon$ is compact, $\mathrm{diam} M_\epsilon \le C Q^{-1/2}$, and $C^{-1} Q \le R(x,0) \le C Q$ on $M_\epsilon$, where $Q=R(x_0,0)$ for some $x_0 \in \partial M_\epsilon$.

nodes.name: Canonical neighborhoods of high-curvature points
nodes.statement: Given $\epsilon, \kappa > 0$ and $\phi$ as above, one can find $r_0 > 0$: if $g_{ij}(t)$ on a closed three-manifold $M$ has $\phi$-almost nonnegative curvature and is $\kappa$-noncollapsed on scales $< r_0$, then for any point $(x_0,t_0)$ with $t_0 \ge 1$ and $Q = R(x_0,t_0) \ge r_0^{-2}$, the solution in $\{(x,t): \mathrm{dist}^2_{t_0}(x,x_0) < (\epsilon Q)^{-1}, t_0 - (\epsilon Q)^{-1} \le t \le t_0\}$ is, after scaling by $Q$, $\epsilon$-close to the corresponding subset of some ancient solution satisfying 11.1.
conclusions: Scaled solution near $(x_0,t_0)$ is $\epsilon$-close to a piece of an ancient solution satisfying 11.1

nodes.name: Curvature bound at fixed time
nodes.statement: Given $\phi$ and any $A>0$ there exists $K(A) < \infty$: if a 3-dim solution has $\phi$-almost nonnegative curvature and satisfies the assumptions of theorem 8.2 with $r_0=1$, then $R(x,1) \le K$ whenever $\mathrm{dist}_1(x,x_0) < A$.
conclusions: $R(x,1) \le K(A)$ for $\mathrm{dist}_1(x,x_0) < A$

nodes.name: Curvature bound from volume hypothesis
nodes.statement: For any $w>0$ there exist $\tau(w), \rho(w) > 0$ and $K(w) < \infty$: if $g_{ij}(t)$ on $M \times [0,T)$ satisfies $Vol B(x_0,r_0) \ge w r_0^n$ and sectional curvatures $\ge -r_0^{-2}$ at $t=t_0$, and is $\phi$-almost nonnegatively curved, then $R(x,t) < K r_0^{-2}$ whenever $t_0 \ge 4\tau r_0^2$, $t \in [t_0 - \tau r_0^2, t_0]$, $\mathrm{dist}_t(x,x_0) \le r_0/4$, provided $\phi(r_0^{-2}) < \rho$.

nodes.name: Volume bound from sectional curvature minimum
nodes.statement: Given $\phi$, for any $w>0$ there exists $\rho > 0$: if $g_{ij}(t)$ is $\phi$-almost nonnegatively curved on a closed three-manifold and $B(x_0,r_0)$ at $t_0 \ge 1$ has $r_0 < \rho$ and $\min_{x\in B(x_0,r_0)} Rm(x,t_0) = -r_0^{-2}$, then $Vol B(x_0,r_0) \le w r_0^n$.

nodes.name: Thick-thin decomposition
nodes.statement: For any $w>0$ there exist $K(w)<\infty$, $\rho(w)>0$ such that for sufficiently large $t$, $M$ admits $M = M_{thick} \cup M_{thin}$ with: (a) for $x \in M_{thick}$, $|\tilde{Rm}| \le K$ in $B(x,\rho(w)\sqrt{t})$ with volume $\ge \frac{1}{10} w (\rho(w)\sqrt{t})^n$; (b) for $y \in M_{thin}$, there is $r=r(y) \in (0,\rho(w)\sqrt{t})$ such that $Rm \ge -r^{-2}$ in $B(y,r)$ and $Vol B(y,r) < w r^n$.
assumptions: $\tilde{Rm}(x,t) \ge -\phi(\tilde R(x,t)) \tilde R(x,t)$ with $\phi \sim 1/\log$ at infinity (Hamilton-Ivey estimate)
conclusions: Existence of thick-thin decomposition with stated curvature/volume properties

nodes.name: Monotonicity of $\bar\lambda$
nodes.statement: $\bar\lambda(g_{ij}) = \lambda(g_{ij}) V^{2/n}(g_{ij})$ is nondecreasing along the Ricci flow whenever it is nonpositive; the monotonicity is strict unless we are on a gradient soliton.
conclusions: $\bar\lambda(g_{ij}(t))$ is nondecreasing
Monotonicity is strict unless $g_{ij}$ is a gradient soliton

nodes.name: Asymptotic behavior of $\mu(g_{ij},\tau)$
nodes.statement: For an arbitrary metric $g_{ij}$ on a closed manifold $M$, the function $\mu(g_{ij},\tau)$ is negative for small $\tau > 0$ and tends to zero as $\tau$ tends to zero.

nodes.name: Monotonicity formula for $\cF$
nodes.statement: $\cF_t = 2 \int |R_{ij} + \nabla_i\nabla_j f|^2 e^{-f} dV$ (1.4).

nodes.name: Monotonicity formula for $\cW$ (3.4)
nodes.statement: $\frac{d\cW}{dt} = \int_M 2\tau |R_{ij} + \nabla_i\nabla_j f - \frac{1}{2\tau} g_{ij}|^2 (4\pi\tau)^{-n/2} e^{-f} dV$.

nodes.name: $\mathcal{L}$-geodesic equation
nodes.statement: $\nabla_X X - \frac{1}{2}\nabla R + \frac{1}{2\tau} X + 2\mathrm{Ric}(X,\cdot) = 0$ (7.2).

nodes.name: Differential inequality for $l$
nodes.statement: $l_{\bar\tau} - \triangle l + |\nabla l|^2 - R + \frac{n}{2\bar\tau} \ge 0$ (7.13); $2\triangle l - |\nabla l|^2 + R + \frac{l-n}{\bar\tau} \le 0$ (7.14).

nodes.name: Hamilton's matrix Harnack inequality
nodes.statement: $R_t + 2 \langle X, \nabla R \rangle + 2 \mathrm{Ric}(X,X) \ge 0$ (11.1) for ancient solutions with nonnegative curvature operator.

nodes.name: Gaussian logarithmic Sobolev inequality
nodes.statement: For probability density $u = (2\pi)^{-n/2} e^{-f}$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$, $\int_{\mathbb{R}^n} [\frac{1}{2}|\nabla f|^2 + f - n] (2\pi)^{-n/2} e^{-f} dx \ge 0$.

nodes.name: Hamilton compactness theorem
nodes.statement: A subsequence of scalings of a Ricci flow with uniformly bounded curvatures and injectivity radii bounded away from zero at the origin converges (modulo diffeomorphisms) to a complete solution to the Ricci flow.

nodes.name: Hamilton-Ivey almost-nonnegative curvature estimate
nodes.statement: In dimension three, normalized curvatures $\tilde{Rm}(x,t) = t Rm(x,t)$ satisfy $\tilde{Rm} \ge -\phi(\tilde R) \tilde R$ with $\phi(\cdot) \sim 1/\log$ at infinity.

nodes.name: Bishop-Gromov volume comparison
nodes.statement: The volume ratio $Vol B(p,r)/Vol_{\mathrm{model}}(r)$ on a manifold with Ricci curvature bounded below is nonincreasing in $r$.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 1.2
nodes.statement: By Cauchy-Schwarz: $\cF_t \ge \frac{2}{n}(\int (R+\triangle f) e^{-f} dV)^2 = \frac{2}{n}\cF^2$, then integrate.

nodes.name: Proof of the claim in 2.3 ($\bar\lambda$ monotonicity)
nodes.statement: Differentiate $\bar\lambda$ along the flow and use the gradient interpretation; combine traceless square plus variance term to obtain $d\bar\lambda/dt \ge 0$.

nodes.name: Proof of claim in 3.1 (asymptotic $\mu$)
nodes.statement: Use a $\delta$-function initial datum for the conjugate heat equation to show $\mu \to 0$ from below; rescale $\frac{1}{2}\tau^{-1} g_{ij}$ to euclidean and contradict the Gaussian log-Sobolev inequality.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 4.1 (no local collapsing I)
nodes.statement: From a collapsing sequence, build cutoff test functions $f_k$ that drive $\mu(g_{ij}(t_k), r_k^2) \to -\infty$; monotonicity of $\mu$ then forces $\mu(g_{ij}(0), t_k+r_k^2) \to -\infty$, contradiction.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 8.2 (no local collapsing II)
nodes.statement: Set $\tau(t)=1-t$, apply Section 7 constructions; control $\bar L$ in a small ball around $x_0$ at $t=1/2$ via the maximum principle on $h(y,t) = \phi(d(y,t)-A(2t-1))(\bar L+2n+1)$ using Lemma 8.3.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 10.1 (pseudolocality)
nodes.statement: Argument by contradiction: localize a point of high curvature, build a conjugate-heat solution from a $\delta$-function there and a cutoff $h$, transfer the $v$-bound to time $0$, and contradict the Gaussian log-Sobolev inequality via spherical symmetrization.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 11.2 (gradient shrinking soliton limit)
nodes.statement: Use estimates from Section 7 to control $l$ and $\tau R$, take a blow-down limit using the $\kappa$-noncollapsing assumption, and exploit the equality cases in (7.12), (7.14) for the reduced volume.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 12.1 (canonical neighborhoods)
nodes.statement: Argument by contradiction: blow up at points of nearly minimal curvature failing the conclusion, prove auxiliary curvature/distance Claims 1-2, extract a smooth limit on $(t',t_0]$, then extend it past $t'$ using the Harnack inequality and Lemma 8.3.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 11.7 (compactness of ancient solutions)
nodes.statement: Show distances at $t=0$ between $x_k$ and high-curvature $y_k$ go to infinity using Corollary 11.5, relative volume comparison, and Shi's local derivative estimates; preclude unbounded curvature via the splitting/cylindrical-neck argument.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 11.4 ($\cV=0$)
nodes.statement: Induction on dimension: in dim 2 vacuous (Cor 11.3); for $n \ge 3$, classify the asymptotic scalar curvature ratio $\cR$ into $\infty$ (dimension reduction), $(0,\infty)$ (cone limit excluded by Hamilton's strong maximum principle), and $0$ (flatness).

nodes.name: Hamilton's surgery procedure (sketch)
nodes.statement: When the Ricci flow develops singularities, replace the tips of the horns by smooth caps and continue running the flow; iterate, with surgeries arising only finitely many times on any finite time interval.
input: Smooth Ricci flow $g_{ij}(t)$ on $M \times [1,T)$ becoming singular as $t \to T$
output: Continued Ricci flow with surgery beyond singular times
Topological reconstruction of $M$ as a connected sum of thick-thin pieces and quotients of $\mathbb{S}^3$, $\mathbb{S}^2 \times \mathbb{R}$

nodes.name: Bochner-Lichnerowicz interpretation of $\cF^m$
nodes.statement: $\cF^m$ has a natural interpretation in terms of modified Bochner-Lichnerowicz formulas with $dm = e^{-f} dV$; $\cF^m = \int g^{ij} R_{ij}^m dm$.

nodes.name: Statistical analogy: $\cW$ as minus entropy
nodes.statement:
Treating $\cW$ as $-S$ for a canonical ensemble at temperature $	au$ with partition function $\log Z = \int (-f + n/2) dm$, one obtains $S = -\int (	au(R+|
abla f|^2) + f - n) dm$ and $\sigma = 2	au^4 \int |R_{ij}+
abla_i
abla_j f -  rac{1}{2	au} g_{ij}|^2 dm \ge 0$.

nodes.name: Riemannian formalism in infinite dimensions
nodes.statement: On $\tilde M = M \times \mathbb{S}^N \times \mathbb{R}^+$ with explicit warped metric, the Ricci tensor vanishes mod $N^{-1}$, and Bishop-Gromov volume comparison on $\tilde M$ yields the reduced volume monotonicity for the Ricci flow on $M$.

nodes.name: Logarithmic Sobolev on shrinking solitons
nodes.statement: The monotonicity formula (3.4) can be used to prove a version of the logarithmic Sobolev inequality with description of equality cases on shrinking Ricci solitons.

nodes.name: Conjecture: uniqueness of noncompact 3D ancient solutions
nodes.statement: There is conjecturally only one (up to scaling) noncompact three-dimensional $\kappa$-noncollapsed ancient solution with bounded positive curvature: Bryant's rotationally symmetric gradient steady soliton.

nodes.name: Characterization of Ricci flow via heat kernels
nodes.statement: Ricci flow is the unique evolution $(g_{ij})_t = A_{ij}$ for which the fundamental solution of the conjugate heat equation satisfies $(\Box \bar f + \bar f/t)(q,t) = o(1)$ near the singular point $(p,0)$; in fact $O(|pq|^2 + |t|)$.

nodes.name: Boundedness of normalized curvature as $t \to \infty$
nodes.statement: Whether the normalized curvatures $\tilde{Rm}(x,t) = t Rm(x,t)$ must stay bounded as $t \to \infty$ for nonsingular Ricci flows, and whether reducible manifolds and manifolds with finite fundamental group can carry metrics evolving smoothly by Ricci flow on the infinite time interval.

nodes.name: Reduce to unit-mass measure
nodes.statement: Assume $\int_M dm = 1$ and write the gradient-flow evolution equations $(g_{ij})_t = -2(R_{ij}+\nabla_i\nabla_j f)$, $f_t = -R - \triangle f$.

nodes.name: Modify by diffeomorphism
nodes.statement:
After modifying by an appropriate diffeomorphism, obtain $(g_{ij})_t = -2R_{ij}$, $f_t = -	riangle f + |
abla f|^2 - R$ and retain $\cF_t = 2\int |R_{ij}+
abla_i
abla_j f|^2 e^{-f} dV$.

nodes.name: Cauchy-Schwarz lower bound
nodes.statement: Compute $\cF_t \ge \frac{2}{n}\int (R+\triangle f)^2 e^{-f} dV \ge \frac{2}{n}(\int (R+\triangle f) e^{-f} dV)^2 = \frac{2}{n}\cF^2$, then integrate the ODE inequality.

nodes.name: Build a degenerate test function
nodes.statement: Take $f_k(x) = -\log\phi(\mathrm{dist}_{t_k}(x,p_k) r_k^{-1}) + c_k$ where $\phi=1$ on $[0,1/2]$, decreasing on $[1/2,1]$, and very small on $[1,\infty)$; $c_k \to -\infty$ as $r_k^{-n} Vol(B_k) \to 0$.

nodes.name: Drive $\mu(g(t_k),r_k^2) \to -\infty$
nodes.statement: Show $\cW(g_{ij}(t_k), f_k, r_k^2) \to -\infty$, hence $\mu(g_{ij}(t_k), r_k^2) \to -\infty$.

nodes.name: Apply monotonicity to reach contradiction
nodes.statement: By monotonicity of $\mu$ along the flow, $\mu(g_{ij}(0), t_k + r_k^2) \to -\infty$, but $t_k+r_k^2$ is bounded so this contradicts continuity at $t=0$.

nodes.name: Reduce to $r_0=1$ and choose $p$
nodes.statement: By scaling assume $r_0=1$ and $\mathrm{dist}_1(x,x_0)=A$; apply the constructions of 7.1 with $p=x$ and $\tau(t)=1-t$.

nodes.name: Translate collapsing into $\tilde V$ smallness
nodes.statement: Mirror the argument of 7.3: collapsing on scale $r \le 1$ at $x$ forces the reduced volume $\tilde V(r^2)$ to be very small, so what is needed is a positive lower bound on $\tilde V(1)$.

nodes.name: Maximum-principle argument on $h$
nodes.statement: Apply the maximum principle to $h(y,t) = \phi(d(y,t)-A(2t-1))(\bar L(y,1-t)+2n+1)$ using Lemma 8.3(a) and (7.15) to bound $\Box h \ge -(2n+C(A))h$, then deduce a lower bound on $\bar L$ in the small ball.

nodes.name: Setup contradiction and locate bad point $(\bar x,\bar t)$
nodes.statement: Assume the conclusion fails for sequences $\epsilon_k,\delta_k \to 0$; using a point-picking argument (Claim 1) construct $(\bar x, \bar t) \in M_\alpha$ with $|Rm|(x,t) \le 4|Rm|(\bar x,\bar t)$ in the prescribed parabolic neighborhood.

nodes.name: Conjugate heat solution and lower bound on $-\int_B v$
nodes.statement: Consider $u = (4\pi(\bar t - t))^{-n/2} e^{-f}$ from a $\delta$-function at $(\bar x, \bar t)$ and the corresponding nonpositive $v$; show $-\int_B v \ge \beta > 0$ for some $\tilde t \in [\bar t - \frac{1}{2}\alpha Q^{-1}, \bar t]$ (Claim 3).

nodes.name: Build cutoff and propagate to $t=0$
nodes.statement: Choose $h(y,t) = \phi(\tilde d(y,t)/(10A\epsilon))$ with $\tilde d = d + 200n\sqrt{t}$; use $\Box h \le 0$-type estimates and (9.1) to obtain $-\int_M h v|_{t=0} \ge \beta(1 - A^{-2})$ and $\int_M h u|_{t=0} \ge 1 - A^{-2}$.

nodes.name: Contradict Gaussian log-Sobolev inequality
nodes.statement: Rescale by $\frac{1}{2}\bar t^{-1}$ and pass to the Euclidean limit to get a sequence of nonnegative $u = (2\pi)^{-n/2} e^{-f}$ with $\int u \to 1$ and $\int [-\frac{1}{2}|\nabla f|^2 - f + n] u$ bounded away from zero, contradicting the Gaussian log-Sobolev inequality (using spherical symmetrization).

nodes.name: Set up blow-down with $q(\tau)$
nodes.statement: Pick $(p,t_0)$ and define $\tilde V(\tau), l(q,\tau)$ as in 7.1 with $\tau(t)=t_0-t$; for each $\tau$ choose $q(\tau)$ with $l(q(\tau),\tau) \le n/2$.

nodes.name: Extract blow-down limit
nodes.statement: Use (7.16) to bound $l(q,\tau)$ and $\tau R(q, t_0-\tau)$ in a parabolic neighborhood and the $\kappa$-noncollapsing to extract $\bar g_{ij}(\tau)$ defined for $\tau \in (1/2,1)$ with $(\bar g_{ij})_\tau = 2 \bar R_{ij}$, and limit $\bar l$ satisfying (7.13), (7.14).

nodes.name: Force equality cases and gradient shrinking soliton
nodes.statement: Since $\tilde V(\tau)$ is nonincreasing and bounded below, the limit $\bar V(\tau)$ is a positive constant strictly less than $(4\pi)^{n/2}$; (7.14) becomes equality so $\bar l$ is smooth, and (7.12) equality forces $\bar R_{ij} + \bar\nabla_i\bar\nabla_j \bar l - \frac{1}{2\tau} \bar g_{ij} = 0$, i.e. a gradient shrinking soliton.

nodes.name: Setup contradiction and choose nearly-minimal $(x_0,t_0)$
nodes.statement: Take $r_0 \to 0$ with conclusion failing; among bad points $(x_0,t_0)$ with $t_0 \ge 1$ pick one with nearly minimal $Q = R(x_0,t_0)$ so that the conclusion holds for all $(x,t)$ with $R(x,t) > 2Q$ in a parabolic neighborhood of size $H Q^{-1}$, $H \to \infty$.

nodes.name: Local curvature/distance Claim 1
nodes.statement: Show $R(x,t) \le 4\bar Q$ for $\bar t - c\bar Q^{-1} \le t \le \bar t$, $\mathrm{dist}_{\bar t}(x,\bar x) \le c\bar Q^{-1/2}$ where $\bar Q = Q + R(\bar x,\bar t)$, using $|R_t| \le C R^2$ and $|\nabla R| \le C R^{3/2}$ from the choice of $(x_0,t_0)$.

nodes.name: Cylindrical structure Claim 2
nodes.statement: Show $\mathrm{dist}_{\bar t}(\bar x, z) \ge A \bar Q^{-1/2}$ for high-curvature points $x$: rescale by $\bar Q$ and analyze two cases (curvature stays bounded along $\gamma$ vs. blows up), the latter producing a non-flat metric cone forbidden by Hamilton's strong maximum principle.

nodes.name: Smooth limit at $t_0$ and extension backward
nodes.statement: Use Claims 1-2 plus $\kappa$-noncollapsing to extract a smooth limit at $t=t_0$ with bounded nonnegative curvature; use Hamilton's Harnack and Lemma 8.3(b) to extend the limit to all $t < t_0$, contradicting the bound in 12.1.

nodes.name: Long-distance separation
nodes.statement: Show distances at $t=0$ between $x_k$ and $y_k$ with $R(y_k,0) \to \infty$ go to infinity: define $z_k$ as the closest point with $R(z_k,0)\mathrm{dist}_0^2(x_k,z_k)=1$, then bound $R(z,0)/R(z_k,0)$ in $B(z_k, 2 R(z_k,0)^{-1/2})$ via 11.5 and Shi's local derivative estimates.

nodes.name: Bounded curvature at $t=0$
nodes.statement: Suppose curvature unbounded at $t=0$; find $y_i \to \infty$ with $R(y_i,0) \to \infty$ and $R(y,0) \le 2R(y_i,0)$ in a large ball; rescale to obtain a limit splitting off a line, hence by Cor 11.3 a round cylinder, contradicting that an open manifold of nonneg curvature cannot contain shrinking cylindrical necks.

nodes.name: Base case $n=2$
nodes.statement: In dimension two, Cor 11.3 says only the round sphere arises, so $\cV = 0$ vacuously.

nodes.name: Trichotomy on asymptotic scalar curvature ratio
nodes.statement: Assume $\cV > 0$ for some $t_0$; consider $\cR = \limsup R(x,t_0) d^2(x)$ as $d(x) \to \infty$ and split into $\cR = \infty$, $0 < \cR < \infty$, $\cR = 0$.

nodes.name: Eliminate each case
nodes.statement: For $\cR = \infty$, blow up to a non-flat ancient solution that splits off a line, applying dimension reduction (induction hypothesis); for $\cR \in (0,\infty)$, blow up to a non-flat metric cone, ruled out by Hamilton's strong maximum principle; for $\cR = 0$, the metric is flat in dimensions $\ge 3$.
